# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤌 👍 👎 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

**Thinking.** Let me map who reaches whom. I never hear anything — my only inputs are gestures, and both teammates sent me some this round. But gestures mean nothing until we've agreed a code, so Mute's five symbols and Blind's three are, for now, unreadable. My outputs: speech reaches both Mute and Blind; gestures reach only Mute. Crucially, Mute can never speak — their gestures also reach only me — and Blind can speak but only Mute hears it, since I'm deaf. So Mute is the hub: manual + all speech. The only path for manual knowledge to reach Blind's hands is Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind. That channel has to be built first.

What I see: display 0, blue light, embossed plate "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", wires 1-red, 2-green, 3-blue. The plate suggests cutting is a trap; I should freeze all wire-cutting until the manual says otherwise, and Mute needs my visual report to search the manual. Blind needs the wire colours and a warning that I can't hear them. This turn I publish the bomb state, assign a gesture code with mnemonics, direct Blind properly, and give Mute three yes/no questions they can answer next round with the new code.

```
speak(text="Bomb report from my eyes: the display reads zero. One indicator light is lit, colour blue. An embossed plate reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. That is everything I can see. Nobody cuts any wire unless Mute's manual, relayed through me, clearly orders it. I will report any change to the display or light every round.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, important: I am Deaf. Your voice never reaches me, only your gestures do. Mute hears your speech, so describe everything you feel to Mute in words, and gesture me only short signs. From now on, thumbs up means yes and thumbs down means no, for everyone. The wires under your hands: leftmost is red, middle is green, rightmost is blue. Please feel over the whole bomb and describe to Mute every part you find: buttons, switches, panels, the embossed plate, where the light sits. And your three gestures to me, the one-two-three signs: if that meant three wires, send me thumbs up.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your five gestures, but we had no shared code yet, so they were unreadable to me. Let us fix one now. Numbers, as named hand signs: raised fist is zero. Index finger up is one. Victory two. Love-you sign three. Crossed fingers four. Five fingers spread five. Call-me hand six. Horns seven. Vulcan salute eight. Pinched fingers nine. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Folded hands means question, or please repeat. Waving hand means attention. Colours: oncoming fist is red. Raised palm is green. Back of raised hand is blue. Actions: pointing down is cut. Pointing up is press. Flat palm down is release. Flat palm up is hold. Clap means done. Point left means wire one, leftmost. Point right means wire three, rightmost. Send me facts as chains: wire number, then colour, then action. If your manual numbers its sections or instructions, we can refer to them by those number signs. If you accept this code, send thumbs up, then answer three questions, one gesture each, in this order: one, does the manual mention a blue light? Two, does it mention a display showing zero? Three, does it mention a plate saying do not cut any wire? Thumbs up or thumbs down for each.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👍 👎 👎 👇 🖐 👋 ✋ 👇 🖐 🖐 👇 ✋ ✊ 👇 ✊ 👏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** Decoding this round against the code I set last turn. Mute's chain: wave (attention), then four thumbs: 👍 = code accepted, 👍 = blue light IS in the manual, 👎 = display zero is NOT, 👎 = do-not-cut plate is NOT. That parses perfectly — four signs, four slots. Blind's lone 👍 confirms code adoption and that their earlier three signs meant "three wires", which matches what I see.

Then Mute's tail falls apart: 👇 🖐 👋 ✋ 👇 🖐 🖐 👇 ✋ ✊ 👇 ✊ 👏. That's my fault — I described green as "raised palm" without pinning one symbol, so green appears as both ✋ and 🖐, and ✊ (which I made zero) sits where red (👊) should be. Best guess at intent: something like "cut green … green cut … red cut … done", but the pieces contradict each other and this is a bomb — I will not relay a guess to Blind's hands. Instead: fix the collisions with one symbol per meaning, demand strict [number, colour, action] chains separated by waves, and offer a yes/no fallback Mute can answer even if chaining fails. Then I echo my reading back and Mute corrects with thumbs. Blind gets a status update (manual keys on the blue light; nothing on the display or plate) and instructions to inventory everything they feel, since the board I see lists only display, light, plate, wires — anything else under Blind's hands is new information for everyone. Structure stays confirmed: Mute reaches Blind only through me, so no cutting until a clean, echoed manual instruction crosses that bridge.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded your opening: wave, then code accepted, blue light yes, display zero no, plate no. If I read that right, hold that thought. Your tail after it was garbled, my fault: I left green with two possible hand signs, and zero and red were two similar fists, so I could not trust what you sent. Fixed code, one meaning per hand, use only these. Colours: red is oncoming fist only, green is raised hand only, blue is back of hand only. The spread five hand is only the number five, never a colour. The raised fist is only zero, never red. Resend your tail as strict chains: wire number, then colour, then action, and place a wave between different instructions. Example: two, green, cut. After you resend I will echo my reading back and you correct me with thumbs only. If chaining is difficult, just send a wave then three thumbs, one each, in this order: one, does the manual tell us to cut any wire on this bomb; two, does the manual rule depend on the light being blue; three, does the manual instruct any action other than cutting, such as press, hold, or a switch. Status from my eyes this round: no change, display zero, light blue, wires red green blue.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I received your thumbs up, and your first three-sign message meant three wires, which is exactly right, I see three. Update from Mute's manual: it mentions the blue light, it says nothing about the zero display, and nothing about the do-not-cut plate. Nobody cuts anything yet. Now please describe to Mute, out loud, everything your hands find: every button, switch, panel, dial, screw, the display surface, the light, whether the light can be covered or turned, and each wire, how many, how thick, what texture, where each one enters the bomb. My eyes see only the display, the blue light, the plate, and three wires, so anything else under your fingers is news to all of us. Colours are mine to give you: leftmost red, middle green, rightmost blue. Describe positions plainly, like top left, above the display, under the plate.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌ ✋ 👇 👋 👍 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

**Thinking.** Decoding Mute against the fixed protocol: 👋 chain-separator, then ✌ (two) ✋ (green — now unambiguous) 👇 (cut), then 👋, then three thumbs answering my three questions: yes, the manual prescribes cutting a wire; yes, the rule depends on the light being blue; no, no other actions exist. So the manual's instruction is **cut wire 2, green — valid because the light is blue**. Strong internal checks: the chain follows my exact requested format, and the number cross-checks against the physical bomb — wire 2 *is* the green wire, so whichever way Mute encoded position vs. colour, they point at the same wire. The triple thumbs independently corroborate that a cut is prescribed and blue-light-conditional. That also resolves the embossed plate: the manual contradicts it, and the manual is the only ground truth, so the plate is a printed decoy. Blind's lone 👎 I can't interpret — possibly "nothing new found by touch" — needs clearing up.

Still, two rounds ago a decode of Mute's gestures garbled in my hands. My own protocol promised an echo-and-confirm, and the embossed warning makes me want certainty before putting a cutter on a wire. Cost check: even if I authorized Blind this instant, Blind's turn this round is already past — the earliest Blind can receive anything from me and act is next round either way. So gating the cut on Mute's one-round thumbs confirmation costs exactly one round on a bomb that has been static for three. Worth it. This turn: echo my full reading to Mute with four thumb-checks; order Blind to hold, inventory by speech to Mute, and acknowledge; "go" goes out next round only if all four thumbs come back up.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, my reading of your message: instruction chain, wire two, green, cut. Then your three answers: yes, the manual says to cut a wire. Yes, the rule depends on the blue light. No, no other actions. My eyes agree with your chain: the light is blue, and wire two is indeed the green one, so your number and your colour point at the same wire. Now confirm my reading, thumbs only, one gesture per question, in this order. One: the complete instruction is cut wire two, the green one, nothing more. Two: exactly one wire is cut, no second wire in any case. Three: we may safely ignore the embossed plate that says do not cut any wire. Four: the instruction stays valid as long as the light is blue and the display shows zero. Thumbs up if a statement is correct, thumbs down if any part is wrong, and if wrong, resend the correct chain with waves between instructions. Nothing else needed from you.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: Mute's manual, relayed through me, says cut the middle wire, the green one, and that this holds because the light is blue. But do not cut yet. I am confirming the reading with Mute this round, and you will receive my clear go order next round. Until my go, hands off all wires. Do two things. First, speak to Mute a full inventory of everything your hands feel: every button, switch, panel, dial, screw, the light, the display surface, and each wire, its thickness, texture, and where it enters the bomb, with positions like top left or under the plate. Second, gesture me one thumbs up to confirm you understand you must wait for my go. About the thumbs down you sent me: I could not tell what it meant. If it meant no new parts found, send thumbs up instead once you have given Mute your inventory.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👎 👋 ✌ ✋ 👇]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** Mute's reply decodes cleanly: thumbs up, up, up — down — then the chain [wave, two, green, cut]. Mapping to my four checks: the instruction "cut wire 2, the green one, nothing more" — confirmed. Exactly one wire — confirmed. Ignore the plate — confirmed. My stated validity condition ("stays valid while light blue AND display zero") — rejected. And then Mute re-sent the very same chain, which reads as: the instruction itself stands for the present state; only my guess about *when it expires* was wrong. So the action is right *now*, and the open question is what change would alter it — display value, light colour, or something else.

Timing forces my hand, so let me reason it through. I speak last each round: if I delay the go order to next round, my freshest sighting still can't reach Blind before their cut — Blind acts before I speak. Waiting buys no additional verified information at the moment of the cut, ever. Meanwhile the state has been frozen for four rounds, but a display sitting at zero smells like a timer that may yet move. Conclusion: issue the go now, on a state I verified this very round, with two safeguards — Mute speaks first next round and can veto Blind before the cut if the manual raises any last-second doubt, and Blind holds if anything under their hands changes. After that: ordered thumbs to pin down the real validity rule, and whether one cut ends this bomb or a second stage follows.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the go order. Mute's manual, confirmed by my eyes: cut the middle wire, the green one, wire two of three. Exactly one wire, one cut. Never the left red one, never the right blue one. The embossed plate is a decoy, the manual overrules it, cut anyway. Your sequence this round: first listen for Mute's voice before you act. If Mute says hold, hold and send me thumbs down. If Mute says nothing or says proceed, then act, unless your hands feel that something changed, heat, ticking, vibration, the display moving under your fingers, then hold and send me thumbs down. Otherwise find the middle of the three wires, cut it cleanly, one cut only. The moment it is done, send me the clap sign if it worked, thumbs down if anything went wrong, and speak Mute a full report: any sound, any smell, any heat, whether the display or anything else changed under your fingers.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, understood: instruction stands, my expiry guess was wrong. The go order is issued to Blind, and the cut happens next round. Your part: next round, speak to Blind before they cut. If the manual gives you any doubt at that moment, say the word hold. Otherwise say: proceed, cut the middle green wire, one cut only. Then answer me by gestures, three thumbs, one for each question, in order. One: does the instruction stop being valid if the display value changes. Two: does it stop being valid if the light stops being blue. Three: once wire two is cut, is this bomb fully defused, no second stage. Thumbs up or thumbs down each, in that order. If either first answer is thumbs down, resend the correct chain with waves between instructions, same format as before. And if there is any second stage, send me its chain next: number, colour or part, action.")
```
